QUESTIONS

Useful things to know.

Can an agent act on our systems?+

Actions can be enabled within an explicitly authorised scope. Sensitive actions need appropriate approval and audit records.

Will AI always answer correctly?+

No. We design evaluation, fallback and human review around the use case, rather than promising error-free outputs.

How are ongoing costs handled?+

Model usage, hosting, integration services and support are scoped separately where appropriate, with agreed limits and monitoring.

IN MORE DETAIL

What can AI automation do for a business?

AI automation combines a model’s ability to interpret or generate information with a controlled business workflow. Examples include drafting support replies, finding approved knowledge, extracting information from documents and routing a task to the right team. A chatbot is one possible interface; a useful automation may also operate behind an internal form or service desk.

The starting point should be a task that can be measured. Record the current process, typical exceptions and the quality threshold. Then choose the data sources, model or tools and approval points. Testing must include cases where the assistant should decline an action, ask for clarification or hand the work to a person. A plausible answer is not the same as a correct business outcome.

Production readiness includes cost limits, provider outages, data retention, permissions and monitoring. Keep privileged actions within a specifically authorised workflow. A customer-facing assistant should have a clear escalation path when it cannot answer reliably. Changes to the model, knowledge sources or connected systems may require new evaluation rather than treating the initial pilot as permanent proof.
